role: SECURITY specialist pass over the frozen tree, after INFRA/BACKEND/DEVOPS
how: an independent read-only reviewer attacked the tree (tenancy per route, cross-tenant reads, egress, traversal, secrets, edge validation) and every finding was re-verified here by hand before being fixed; the fixes carry regression tests in tests/test_tenancy_and_security.py

findings.what: app/actions/mcp_adapter.py dispatched the inner capability with the arguments only, so the handler never saw the authenticated tenant and fell back to a hard-coded "local" (app/actions/{project_knowledge_grounding,voice_gateway,mcp_adapter,outcome_capture_and_ledger,local_drive}.py). A caller with a second brokerage's token could reach the first tenant's corpus, ledger chain and drive root through POST /v1/mcp tools/call.
findings.fix: the adapter now forwards the principal's tenant into the inner handler ({**clean, "tenant_id": tenant_id}) exactly as the HTTP envelope does, and all five handlers refuse with "tenant_id is required" instead of inventing one

findings.what: app/domain.webhook_delivery checked the caller's URL with check_egress and then used urllib.request.urlopen, which follows 3xx by default: a public host answering 302 Location: http://169.254.169.254/... moved the platform onto the link-local network after the guard had approved the first hop.
findings.fix: the delivery uses an opener with a guarded redirect handler that re-applies check_egress to every hop and refuses the delivery when a hop is refused

findings.what: app/auth.json_object read the whole body with await request.body() and only then compared its length to MAX_BODY_BYTES, so a large body was buffered before being refused (and the public Twilio webhooks read their body before authentication).
findings.fix: the declared Content-Length is refused up front and the body is read chunk by chunk, stopping at the cap; the raw bytes are cached so a route that reads its body twice (a webhook that resolves its tenant from the form and then parses it) does not meet "Stream consumed"

held: no token -> 401 on every /v1 route; another tenant's record -> 404 (never 403, never the record); a tenant named in a payload -> 422
local_drive and storage refuse a relative path that escapes the tenant root, and absolute paths outside it
the egress guard refuses file://, http://127.0.0.1, ::1 and 169.254.169.254 for the URL the caller supplies (the redirect hop was the hole, now closed)
no credential literal in app/**: the platform ships with no Twilio, Google, CRM or model credentials, and each one is named as a setting in README.md
malformed JSON, a non-object body, an over-long field name, a wrong type and an out-of-vocabulary value are all refused with 422 naming the field
not_run: the reviewer could not execute Python (read-only sandbox unavailable), so its findings were static traces; each was reproduced here by hand and the fixes are covered by tests that were run

no container build was possible on this host: docker_health_200 and postgres_boot_200 stay unmeasured until the Store gate boots the image. The Postgres code path was exercised by hand (DATABASE_URL set -> engine dials psycopg v3 -> connection refused by the bogus host, instead of ModuleNotFoundError: psycopg2)
